extracts.title: Ṭihrānī: revelation, reason, and the disputed proof of prophetic necessity
extracts.author: Hāshim al-Ḥusaynī al-Ṭihrānī
extracts.section: Tawḍīḥ al-murād, I, 643–644, necessity of prophetic missions
extracts.arabic:
قول المصنف: وهي واجبة لاشتمالها الخ — يدل هذا الكلام أن للإنسان تكاليف عقلية وتكاليف سمعية، وهو المشهور. ولكن المفيد رحمه الله تعالى قال في أوائل المقالات: إن العقل لا ينفك عن سمع وإن التكليف لا يصح إلا بالرسل، واتفقت الإمامية على أن العقل يحتاج في علمه ونتائجه إلى السمع، وأنه غير منفك عن سمع ينبه الغافل على كيفية الاستدلال، وأنه لا بد في أول التكليف وابتدائه في العالم من رسول.
أقول: الحق مع المفيد رحمه الله وإن خالفه أقوام حتى بعض الإمامية بظاهر كلامهم، لأن العقل البشري له مقام القبول والاستعداد فلا بد له في مقام الحكم والاستدلال من تنبيه وإفاضة من العالين ولو قبل هذه النشأة، وأما الأشاعرة فيعزلون العقل بالكلية على أصلهم كما مر.
قول الشارح: بأن التكاليف السمعية الخ — إيضاح هذا الاستدلال أن الإنسان بمجرد عقله يعمل بالتكاليف العقلية، ولكن الشرع إذا أتى بالتكاليف الأخرى وواظب الإنسان عليها كان للعمل بالتكاليف العقلية أقرب وأحفظ فيحصل اللطف في حكم العقل بالشرع.
أقول: هذا الاستدلال لضعفه لا يقوم على ساق، والحق أن علة وجوب البعثة هي علة حسنها، وهي تلك الفوائد التي أنهاها المصنف إلى قوله: فيحصل اللطف للمكلف.
extracts.english:
[Ṭihrānī introducing the author's lemma:] 'It [the prophetic mission] is obligatory because it includes ...' This implies that human beings have rational duties and duties known through revelation, as is commonly held. However, al-Mufīd said in Awāʾil al-maqālāt that reason is never without hearing [revealed teaching], and that imposition of duty is not sound except through messengers. He reports the Imāmī agreement that reason needs revealed instruction for its knowledge and results, and requires a message that alerts the heedless to the manner of inference, so that at the beginning of religious obligation there must be a messenger.

[Ṭihrānī:] I say that al-Mufīd is right, despite dissent, even among some Imāmīs in the apparent sense of their remarks. For human reason occupies a state of receptivity and preparedness; in judging and inferring it therefore needs an awakening and effusion from higher beings, even if that occurs before this earthly life. The Ashʿarīs, by contrast, exclude reason entirely according to their principle, as discussed earlier.

[Explaining the commentator's argument:] A human being observes rational duties by reason alone. But if religious law brings further duties and a person perseveres in them, that person comes closer to and better preserves the performance of rational duties. Thus revelation becomes a gracious assistance (luṭf) to rational judgment.

[Ṭihrānī:] I say: This argument is too weak to stand. Rather, the reason that prophetic missions are obligatory is the same reason they are good: the benefits that the author itemized up to his words 'and grace is thereby realized for the responsible person'.
notes: These paragraphs cover the page break between printed pp. 643–644. This is a dispute WITHIN the discussion of prophetic missions; not a blanket claim that unveiled mystical experience displaces rational proof. Ṭihrānī explicitly endorses al-Mufīd on reason's need for guidance yet rejects the commentator's narrower argument for prophetic necessity. His claim about Ashʿarīs is a polemical attribution, not a neutral fact about all Sunni theology. The initial al-Mufīd text is quoted here in Ṭihrānī's reporting; direct verification against Awāʾil al-maqālāt remains outstanding.
extracts.source_line: Hāshim al-Ḥusaynī al-Ṭihrānī, Tawḍīḥ al-murād, I, printed pp. 643–644; section “fī wujūb al-biʿtha”.

extracts.title: Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī: knowledge by illumination and the absence of a veil
extracts.author: Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī
extracts.arabic:
إذا كان عدم الحجاب كافيا في العلم الإشراقي الحضوري، ونور الأنوار نور محض، لا يمكن احتجابه عن ذاته ولا احتجاب غيره من الموجودات العقلية والحسية عنه. فنور الأنوار ظاهر لذاته، أي مدرك لها، على ما سبق بيانه في كل مجرد، وغيره ظاهر له، فيكون مدركا له، «لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض» إذ لا يحجبه شيء عن شيء.
وإذ لم يحجبه شيء عن شيء، فيدرك جميع الأشياء بالإشراق الحضوري، الذي هو أشرف أنحاء الإدراك، لا بصور في ذاته، فيتكثر ذاته المقدسة وجهاته، لكونه فاعلا وقابلا، مع أن جهة الفعل غير جهة القبول، فلا يكون واحدا حقيقيا.
extracts.english:
If the absence of a veil suffices for illuminative, presentational knowledge, and the Light of Lights is pure light, it cannot be veiled from itself, nor can other intelligible and sensible existents be veiled from it. Thus the Light of Lights is manifest to itself—that is, knows itself, as explained previously for every immaterial being—and other things are manifest to it, and therefore known by it: 'Not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or the earth escapes Him,' since nothing conceals one thing from Him by another.

Since nothing conceals any thing from Him, He knows all things through knowledge by presence and illumination, the noblest mode of cognition, not through forms inhering in His essence. Were such forms to inhere in Him, His sacred essence and aspects would be multiplied, because He would be both agent and recipient, although the aspect of acting differs from that of receiving; He would no longer be genuinely one.
notes: This is a *parallel Illuminationist primary source* from a commentary on Suhrawardī's Ḥikmat al-ishrāq, not a Tajrīd ḥāshiya. The chapter opening on this same page discusses visual perception and the elimination of the opacity/barrier model; this bounded argument is the theological application. Printed text on web is a mixed commentary context: a close critical edition must compare the base lemma with the Shīrāzī gloss before assigning each sentence exclusively to Shīrāzī.
extracts.source_line: Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī, Sharḥ Ḥikmat al-ishrāq, printed p. 346, ch. 10.

extracts.title: Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī: a disposition to know is not actual knowledge
extracts.author: Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī
extracts.arabic: فإن ما يجد الإنسان من نفسه عند عرض المسائل علم بالقوة يجد من نفسه ملكة وقدرة على الجواب لهذه المسائل المذكورة. وهذه القوة أقرب إلى الوجود مما كانت، أي من القوة التي كانت قبل السؤال، فإن للقوة مراتب بحسب البعد والقرب من الوجود، ولا يكون للإنسان علما بجواب كل واحد من تلك المسائل على الخصوص ما لم يكن عنده صورة كل واحد واحد. وواجب الوجود منزه عن هذه الأشياء: حلول الصورة فيه، وكون علمه بالقوة، فلا يكون علمه بالموجودات على الوجه المذكور.
extracts.english: What someone discovers within himself when questions are put to him is knowledge in potency: he finds a habitual disposition and capacity to answer those questions. This potency is nearer actuality than before the question was posed, since potencies have degrees according to their remoteness from, or nearness to, existence. But one does not have distinct knowledge of the answer to every single one of those questions unless one possesses its particular form. The Necessary Existent is exempt from all these features: the inherence of a form within Him and the possession of knowledge only potentially. His knowledge of existents cannot take the form just described.
notes: The passage distinguishes (a) potency prior to being asked, (b) acquired readiness/habit (malaka, qudra), and (c) determinate actual knowledge. 'Quwwa' here is cognitive potency, and 'qudra' the capacity to answer, not the same technical meaning. Compare with Suhrawardī base text and Shahrāzūrī before attributing the wording of each lemma to Quṭb. The preceding passage on p. 349 argues that actual knowledge of a necessary concomitant is not automatically the actual knowledge of what it entails.
extracts.source_line: Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī, Sharḥ Ḥikmat al-ishrāq, printed p. 349.

extracts.title: al-Taftāzānī: the common concept of existence and the competing ontologies
extracts.author: Saʿd al-Dīn al-Taftāzānī
extracts.section: Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid, digital pp. 61; conception of existence and the existence/essence problem
extracts.arabic:
قال: البحث الثاني: المنقول عن الشيخ أبي الحسن الأشعري أن وجود كل شيء عين ذاته، وليس للفظ الوجود مفهوم واحد مشترك بين الوجودات، بل الاشتراك لفظي. والجمهور على أن له مفهوما واحدا مشتركا بين الوجودات، إلا أنه عند المتكلمين حقيقة واحدة تختلف بالقيود والإضافات، حتى أن وجود الواجب هو كونه في الأعيان على ما يعقل من كون الإنسان، وإنما الاختلاف في الماهية، فالوجود معنى زائد على الماهية في الواجب والممكن جميعا. وعند الفلاسفة وجود الواجب مخالف لوجود الممكن في الحقيقة، واشتراكهما في مفهوم الكون اشتراك معروضين في لازم خارجي غير مقوم، وهو في الممكن زائد على الماهية عقلا، وفي الواجب نفس الماهية، بمعنى أنه لا ماهية للواجب سوى الوجود الخاص المجرد عن مقارنة الماهية، بخلاف الإنسان فإن له ماهية هو الحيوان الناطق ووجودا هو الكون في الأعيان.
فوقع البحث في ثلاث مقامات: أنه مشترك معنى، وأنه زائد ذهنا، وأنه في الواجب زائد أيضا. والإنصاف أن الأولين بديهيان، والمذكور في معرض الاستدلال تنبيهات. فعلى الأول وجوه: الأول أنا إذا نظرنا في الحادث جزمنا بأن له مؤثرا مع التردد في كونه واجبا أو ممكنا، عرضا أو جوهرا، متحيزا وغير متحيز، ومع تبدل اعتقاد كونه ممكنا إلى اعتقاد كونه واجبا إلى غير ذلك من الخصوصيات، فبالضرورة يكون الأمر المقطوع به الباقي مع التردد في الخصوصيات وتبدل الاعتقادات مشتركا بين الكل.
extracts.english:
[The section introduces a reported position:] The view transmitted from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī is that the existence of each thing is identical with that thing's essence and that 'existence' has no one concept shared by existents; the word is common only by homonymy. The majority maintain that it has one concept common to existents. According to the theologians, however, it is one reality differentiated by qualifications and relations, such that the Necessary's existence is His being in the external world, just as one understands a human being's existence. The difference lies in quiddity: existence is additional to the quiddity of the Necessary and of the possible alike. According to the philosophers, the Necessary's existence differs in reality from possible existence; their shared concept of 'being' pertains to subjects possessing a non-constitutive concomitant. In possibles, existence is intellectually additional to quiddity; in the Necessary it is His very essence, meaning He has no quiddity beyond His specific existence, unmixed with any other quiddity. A human being, by contrast, has the quiddity 'rational animal' and existence as being in the external world.

Three questions arise: whether existence has one meaning; whether it is additional in intellect; and whether it is also additional in the Necessary. Fairness demands that the first two are self-evident; the arguments advanced are reminders. The first reminder for shared meaning is that, upon considering a newly arisen thing, we are certain that it has an agent while remaining undecided whether that agent is necessary or possible, accident or substance, spatial or non-spatial; our opinion of these particularities may change. Necessarily, then, what remains certain throughout these doubts and changes is common to all the alternatives.
notes: SOURCE AND VOICE: “al-manqūl ʿan al-Shaykh Abī al-Ḥasan” explicitly attributes the first view to al-Ashʿarī as reported by al-Taftāzānī; it is NOT a direct quotation from al-Ashʿarī. The “majority,” “theologians” and “philosophers” are a doxographical map offered by al-Taftāzānī, not uniformly accepted self-descriptions. The first reminder supports a shared concept/predicable and does NOT by itself prove the identity of extramental realities. The following printed page explicitly warns that none of these proofs demonstrates that real existences are ontically identical. The final two reminders, further objection/reply and printed edition collation remain to be incorporated in full. Digital page 61 identified on Usul.ai, edition metadata first edition 1401/1981; printed pagination has not been independently checked against facsimile.

extracts.title: al-Taftāzānī: the alleged regress of existence and the intellectual mode of addition
extracts.author: Saʿd al-Dīn al-Taftāzānī
extracts.section: Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid, digital p. 69; answer to substrate/accident regress objections
extracts.arabic:
وأما تفصيلا فعن الأول أن قيامه بالماهية من حيث هي هي، لا بالماهية المعدومة ليلزم التناقض، ولا بالماهية الموجودة ليلزم الدور أو التسلسل. فإن قيل: إن أريد بالماهية من حيث هي هي ما لا يكون الوجود أو العدم نفسها ولا جزءا منها على ما قيل فغير مفيد، لأن العروض كاف في لزوم المحالات؛ وإن أريد ما لا يكون موجودا ولا معدوما لا بالعروض ولا بغيره فالتناقض فيه أظهر، لأن اللاوجود نقيض الوجود بلا نزاع ولا اشتباه. قلنا: المراد ما لا يعتبر فيه الوجود ولا العدم، وإن كان لا ينفك عن أحدهما في الخارج.
فإن قيل: عدم الانفكاك عن أحدهما كاف في لزوم المحال، لأنه إن قارن العدم فيناقض أو الوجود فيدور أو يتسلسل. قلنا: قيام الوجود بالماهية أمر عقلي، ليس كقيام البياض بالجسم ليلزم تقدمها عليه بالوجود تقدما ذاتيا أو زمانيا فتلزم المحالات، بل غاية الأمر أنه يلزم تقدمها عليه بالوجود العقلي ولا استحالة فيه، لجواز أن تلاحظ وحدها من غير ملاحظة وجود خارجي أو ذهني، ويكون لها وجود ذهني لا بملاحظة العقل؛ فإن عدم الاعتبار غير اعتبار العدم. وإن اعتبر العقل وجودها الذهني لم يلزم التسلسل، بل ينقطع بانقطاع الاعتبار.
وعن الثاني أنا نختار أن الوجود موجود ولا نسلم لزوم التسلسل؛ وإنما يلزم لو كان وجوده أيضا زائدا عليه وليس كذلك، بل وجوده عينه وإنما النزاع في غيره، والأدلة إنما قامت عليه. وتحقيق ذلك أنه لما كان تحقق كل شيء بالوجود فبالضرورة يكون تحققه بنفسه من غير احتياج إلى وجود آخر يقوم به، كما أنه لما كان التقدم والتأخر فيما بين الأشياء بالزمان كانا فيما بين أجزائه بالذات من غير افتقار إلى زمان آخر. فإن قيل فيكون كل وجود واجبا إذ لا معنى له سوى ما يكون تحققه بنفسه. قلنا ممنوع، فإن معنى وجود الواجب بنفسه أنه مقتضى ذاته من غير احتياج إلى فاعل، ومعنى تحقق الوجود بنفسه أنه إذا حصل للشيء إما من ذاته كما في الواجب أو من غيره كما في الممكن لم يفتقر تحققه إلى وجود آخر يقوم به.
extracts.english:
In reply to the first objection, the inherence of existence pertains to the quiddity as such: not to a nonexistent quiddity (which would be contradictory), nor to an already existent one (which would cause a circle or an infinite regress). An objector presses: If 'quiddity as such' only means that neither existence nor nonexistence is identical with it or part of it, that does not solve the paradox; and if it means a quiddity neither existent nor nonexistent in any sense, that is yet more contradictory. We answer that neither existence nor nonexistence is being taken into consideration, although in external reality the thing cannot be without one or the other.

The objector replies that this inseparability is enough to restore the paradox: if nonexistence accompanies it, there is contradiction; if existence does, there is circularity or regress. We answer: existence's 'inherence' in quiddity is an affair of intellect, not like whiteness's inherence in a body, which would entail that the substrate has priority of existence, whether essentially or temporally. At most the quiddity has priority in intellectual consideration, and there is nothing impossible about this. The intellect may consider it alone, without considering its external or mental existence, even while it has mental existence independently of that particular act of considering. For *not considering* something is different from *considering its absence*. And if the intellect considers its mental existence in turn, this does not force a real infinite regress: it ends when the act of considering ends.

As to the second objection, we can affirm that existence itself exists without conceding a regress. The regress would follow only if its existence too were additional to it, which it is not; its existence is identical with itself. The disagreement concerns other things, to which the proofs pertain. Since all things are actual through existence, existence necessarily is actual through itself without requiring another existence inhering in it—just as, although priority and posteriority among things are by time, those relations among time's own parts are by time's very essence, without requiring a further time. If one then objects that each existence would be necessary because each is actual through itself, we reject the inference. For the Necessary to exist through itself is for existence to be demanded by its essence without need of an agent. For existence itself to be actual through itself merely means that, whether it comes to a thing from its essence (as with the Necessary) or from another (as with a possible), its actuality needs no second existence inhering in it.
notes: STRUCTURE: direct response to two opposite attempts to treat the existential addition like a real accident in a previously actual subject. Taftāzānī makes the unconsidered/nonexistent distinction precise: ʿadam al-iʿtibār ≠ iʿtibār al-ʿadam. He also sharply differentiates (i) being self-actualizing in the sense of existence's not needing another 'existence' and (ii) the Necessary's causal independence. These are central checks on loose analogies between vertical preservation, participation and formal mediation. Digital Arabic source p. 69 has an unpunctuated transcription; punctuation and paragraphing here are editorial. The surrounding objections are on p. 68, and a further continuation follows the selected excerpt on p. 69; neither should be treated as included in this bounded unit.
extracts.source_line: al-Taftāzānī, Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid, digital numbered p. 69, response to existence/quiddity regress (Usul.ai, metadata first ed. 1401/1981).

extracts.title: On the circularity of alleged definitions
extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: وهذه الحدود كلها باطلة لاشتمالها على الدور، فإن الثابت مرادف للموجود، والمنفي للمعدوم.
extracts.english: All these definitions are invalid because they involve circularity: “established” is synonymous with “existent,” and “negated” with “nonexistent.”

extracts.title: Intrinsic necessity, possibility, impossibility
extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: إذا أخذنا الوجوب والامتناع والامكان على أنها ذاتية لا بالنظر إلى الغير كانت المعقولات منقسمة إليها قسمة حقيقية.
extracts.english: When necessity, impossibility, and possibility are considered intrinsically rather than in relation to another, intelligibles are divided among them by a genuine exhaustive division.
extracts.source_line: al-Ḥillī | Direct Tajrīd commentary | printed p. 68, edition with Ḥasan Zādeh Āmulī annotation. Arabic: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/3439/68?lang=ar
notes: The page also distinguishes lexical explanation from genuine definition; only the directly relevant modal conclusion is quoted.
extracts.role: new concise primary quotation; checked online; not a full continuous argumentative unit

extracts.title: Continued possible existence still needs an effective cause
extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: ذهب جمهور الحكماء والمتأخرين من المتكلمين إلى أن الممكن الباقي محتاج إلى المؤثر.
extracts.english: The majority of philosophers and later theologians maintained that a possible being which persists still needs an efficient cause.
extracts.source_line: al-Ḥillī | Direct Tajrīd commentary | printed p. 117, edition with Ḥasan Zādeh Āmulī annotation. Arabic: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/3439/117?lang=ar
notes: Only al-Ḥillī’s identifying statement is excerpted. His report of the opposing claim, including the abandoned-builder analogy, is paraphrased in the accompanying editorial analysis; the modern printed footnote is not a medieval text.
extracts.role: new concise primary quotation; checked online; not a full continuous argumentative unit

extracts.title: Unity as an intellectual consideration
extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: فإذن الوحدة أمر عقلي اعتباري يحصل في العقل عند فرض عدم انقسام الملحوق.
extracts.english: Thus unity is an intellectual consideration arising in the intellect upon supposing the subject to be undivided.
extracts.source_line: al-Ḥillī | Direct Tajrīd commentary | printed p. 149, edition with Ḥasan Zādeh Āmulī annotation. Arabic: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/3439/149?lang=ar
notes: The excerpt illustrates a premise of the fuller discussion of unity and plurality, without proving all relational categories conceptual.
extracts.role: new concise primary quotation; checked online; not a full continuous argumentative unit

extracts.title: The division of causes begins with dependence
extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: العلة هي ما يحتاج الشئ إليه، وهي إما أن تكون جزءا من المعلول أو خارجة عنه.
extracts.english: A cause is that on which a thing depends; it is either a part of the effect or external to it.
extracts.source_line: al-Ḥillī | Direct Tajrīd commentary | printed p. 169, edition with Ḥasan Zādeh Āmulī annotation. Arabic: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/3439/169?lang=ar
notes: The page proceeds to material, formal, efficient and final causes. The exact small proposition is reproduced; the rest is summarised.
extracts.role: new concise primary quotation; checked online; not a full continuous argumentative unit

extracts.title: Voluntary agency has cognitive prerequisites
extracts.author: al-Ṭūsī (quoted by al-Ḥillī)
extracts.arabic: والفاعل منا يفتقر إلى تصور جزئي ليتخصص الفعل ثم شوق ثم إرادة ثم حركة من العضلات ليقع منا الفعل.
extracts.english: Our acting agent needs a particular conception specifying the action, then desire, then will, and then motion of the muscles for the act to occur.
extracts.source_line: al-Ṭūsī (quoted by al-Ḥillī) | Direct Tajrīd commentary | printed p. 187, edition with Ḥasan Zādeh Āmulī annotation. Arabic: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/3439/187?lang=ar
notes: This is explicitly the lemma from Ṭūsī introduced by al-Ḥillī; speaker is Ṭūsī here, and it is used to elucidate the human causal sequence, not as al-Ḥillī’s invented words.
extracts.role: new concise primary quotation; checked online; not a full continuous argumentative unit

extracts.title: Soul as first perfection of an instrumental body
extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: فالنفس من القسم الأول وهي كمال لجسم طبيعي آلي تصدر عنه أفعاله بواسطة الآلات.
extracts.english: The soul belongs to the first kind [of perfection]: it is the perfection of a natural instrumental body whose acts proceed through its instruments.
extracts.source_line: al-Ḥillī | Direct Tajrīd commentary | printed p. 275, edition with Ḥasan Zādeh Āmulī annotation. Arabic: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/3439/275?lang=ar
notes: Main commentary rather than adjacent modern-editor annotations; excerpt excludes further qualifications about the human soul.
extracts.role: new concise primary quotation; checked online; not a full continuous argumentative unit

extracts.title: Identity despite bodily replacement
extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: فالبدن دائما في التحلل والاستخلاف والهوية باقية من أول العمر إلى آخره والمتبدل مغاير للباقي.
extracts.english: The body is continually dissolved and replenished, while identity persists from the beginning of life to its end; what changes is other than what remains.
extracts.source_line: al-Ḥillī | Direct Tajrīd commentary | printed p. 277, edition with Ḥasan Zādeh Āmulī annotation. Arabic: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/3439/277?lang=ar
notes: This is an argument from persistence of identity against identifying the soul with the changing body; not a complete proof of immortality.
extracts.role: new concise primary quotation; checked online; not a full continuous argumentative unit

extracts.title: What an agent brings about
extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: فليس السواد سوادا بالفاعل بل وجوده وعدمه بالفاعل.
extracts.english: Blackness is not blackness *by* the agent; rather, its existence and nonexistence are by the agent.
extracts.source_line: al-Ḥillī | Direct Tajrīd commentary | printed p. 210, edition with Ḥasan Zādeh Āmulī annotation. Arabic: https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/3439/210?lang=ar
notes: Read with the explicit distinction between causes of quiddity and causes of existence. The causal thesis must not be conflated with al-Taftāzānī’s semantics of existence.
extracts.role: new concise primary quotation; checked online; not a full continuous argumentative unit

extracts.title: A kalām proof of the world’s temporal origination
extracts.author: al-Miqdād al-Siyūrī
extracts.arabic: وثبت أنّ كلّ جسم لا يخلو من الحوادث، وكلّ ما لا يخلو من الحوادث فهو حادث بالضّرورة.
extracts.english: It is established that no body is free of originated events, and that what cannot be free of originated events is necessarily originated.
extracts.source_line: al-Miqdād al-Siyūrī | al-Iʿtimād fī sharḥ Wājib al-iʿtiqād | printed p. 51 | https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9146/51?lang=ar
notes: Not a Tajrīd commentary. A short quotation expressing two premises; its controversial principle requires independent demonstration.

extracts.title: Public prophetic signs and warranted testimony
extracts.author: al-Māwardī
extracts.arabic: والمعجزات من القول هو الإخبار عن غائب لا يعلم به غير مخبره فيكون على صدقه دليلا.
extracts.english: Among verbal miracles is reporting an unseen matter known to no one except its announcer, such that it serves as evidence for his truthfulness.
extracts.source_line: al-Māwardī | Aʿlām al-nubuwwa | printed p. 111 | https://ablibrary.net/book_content/b/9174/111?lang=ar
notes: An independent account of prophetic verification, not a gloss on the Tajrīd; a short selected sentence, not the entire proof.

extracts.title: Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid — supports
extracts.author: Saʿd al-Dīn al-Taftāzānī
extracts.arabic: إذا قلنا: العالم حادث، فالحاصل في الذهن صورة العالم وصورة الحدوث
extracts.english: When we say “the world is originated,” what occurs in the mind is a representation of the world and a representation of origination.
extracts.source_line: Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid, vol. I, p.344 (ʿUmayra ed.) (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: The representation required for judgment is not identical with the extramental subject judged. EDITORIAL LIMIT: We quote the argument in its mental-representation context, not as proof of extra-mental mental forms.

extracts.title: Shawāriq al-ilhām — distinction
extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.arabic: والحمل أي الإيجابي يستدعى اتحاد الطرفين من وجه أي ذاتا ووجودا وتغايرهما من وجه آخر أي مفهوما
extracts.english: Affirmative predication requires agreement between its two terms in one respect—underlying reality and existence—and difference in another respect, namely conception.
extracts.source_line: Shawāriq al-ilhām, vol. I, p.124 (Mahdawī printing) (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: A truthful affirmative predication neither fuses the intensions nor wholly detaches the subject and predicate. EDITORIAL LIMIT: The page explains predication in different senses; quote is not a doctrine of mystical identity.

extracts.title: Shawāriq al-ilhām — definition
extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.arabic: وأما نفس الأمر فمعناه نفس الشيء في حد ذاته على أن يكون المراد بالأمر هو الشيء نفسه
extracts.english: As for nafs al-amr, it means the thing itself as it is in its own right, taking amr to designate the thing itself.
extracts.source_line: Shawāriq al-ilhām, vol. I, p.122 (Mahdawī printing) (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: The standard of truth is not equivalent to “outside the mind”: its independence is from the act of stipulating or imagining. EDITORIAL LIMIT: The claim does not establish an independently existent third realm.

extracts.title: Shawāriq al-ilhām — example
extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.arabic: إنما حكمت بكون الأربعة زوجا لأن الأربعة في حد ماهيتها زوج وليس حال الزوجية بالقياس إلى الخمسة كذلك
extracts.english: I judged four to be even because four is even in the constitution of its quiddity; matters are not so with the alleged evenness of five.
extracts.source_line: Shawāriq al-ilhām, vol. I, p.123 (Mahdawī printing) (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: The truth-making relation is not the psychological act of judgment; otherwise stipulating that five is even would make it true. EDITORIAL LIMIT: The same page reports Jurjānī and Dawwānī in a separate dispute over identification with the Active Intellect.

extracts.title: Shawāriq al-ilhām — claim
extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.arabic: فالجمهور على أن وجود الممكن وعدمه بالنظر إلى ذاته على السواء ولا أولوية لأحدهما على الآخر
extracts.english: The majority maintain that, considered in itself, a possible thing is equally related to existence and nonexistence; neither has intrinsic priority.
extracts.source_line: Shawāriq al-ilhām, vol. I, p.90 (Mahdawī printing) (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: Possibility is an indifference thesis, not a weak propensity to exist. EDITORIAL LIMIT: Other philosophers distinguish a nonnecessitating intrinsic preference; p.91 analyzes objections.

extracts.title: Shawāriq al-ilhām — objection
extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.arabic: والحق إن استلزام الوقوع بلا سبب خارج لكون الواقع واجبا أو ممتنعا غير ضروري
extracts.english: It is not self-evident that occurrence without an external cause would make the occurring thing necessary or impossible.
extracts.source_line: Shawāriq al-ilhām, vol. I, p.91 (Mahdawī printing) (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: The status of awlawiyya needs an argument; it cannot simply be dismissed as logically incoherent at the outset. EDITORIAL LIMIT: Lāhījī subsequently argues against the hypothesis; this sentence alone does not mean he endorses uncaused occurrence.

extracts.title: Shawāriq al-ilhām — reports disagreement
extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.arabic: فذهب الحكماء والمحققون من متأخري المتكلمين إلى أنها الإمكان والقدماء منهم إلى أنَّها الحدوث
extracts.english: The philosophers and critical later theologians held that the ground of needing a cause is possibility; earlier theologians held that it is origination.
extracts.source_line: Shawāriq al-ilhām, vol. I, p.89 (Mahdawī printing) (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: Need because possible versus need because temporally originated are logically different claims. EDITORIAL LIMIT: Later passage gives an argument and counters the claim that both possibility and origination are co-conditions.

extracts.title: Tajrīd / Kashf al-murād — lemma
extracts.author: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī, quoted by al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: والممكن الباقي مفتقر إلى المؤثر لوجود علته
extracts.english: A possible existent that endures continues to need an effective cause because the basis of its need persists.
extracts.source_line: Tajrīd / Kashf al-murād, p.117, Ḥasanzāda Āmulī ed. (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: Continuous causal dependence tracks possibility, which persists, not temporal commencement, which does not repeat. EDITORIAL LIMIT: The lemma is Ṭūsī’s; detailed ensuing discussion is al-Ḥillī or modern editor (must be separated).

extracts.title: Tajrīd / Kashf al-murād — lemma
extracts.author: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī, quoted by al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: والغاية علة بماهيتها لعلية العلة الفاعلية، معلولة في وجودها للمعلول
extracts.english: The end, by what it is, causes the efficient cause to be a cause; in its accomplished existence it is an effect of the produced thing.
extracts.source_line: Tajrīd / Kashf al-murād, p.198, Ḥasanzāda Āmulī ed. (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: The final cause is first in conception and last in realization; explanatory priority is not chronological priority. EDITORIAL LIMIT: For clarity the English is an explanatory rendering; al-Ḥillī’s ensuing house/shelter example supports it.

extracts.title: Tajrīd / Kashf al-murād — lemma
extracts.author: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī, quoted by al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: والضرورة قاضية باستناد أفعالنا إلينا
extracts.english: Immediate recognition demands that our actions be attributable to us.
extracts.source_line: Tajrīd / Kashf al-murād, p.423, Ḥasanzāda Āmulī ed. (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: The direct claim is about attribution of actions; it does not settle every account of divine production or created efficiency. EDITORIAL LIMIT: The modern editor’s added account of God alone bringing actions into existence is distinct and must not be assigned to al-Ḥillī.

extracts.title: Tajrīd / Kashf al-murād — lemma
extracts.author: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī, quoted by al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: ولا يقتضي ذلك ثبوت مادة سوى الجسم لاستحالة التسلسل ووجود ما لا يتناهى
extracts.english: It does not follow that there is matter distinct from body, owing to the impossibility of regress and an actually infinite multitude.
extracts.source_line: Tajrīd / Kashf al-murād, p.229, Ḥasanzāda Āmulī ed. (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: The continuity and indefinite divisibility of body are not a proof of a separate material substrate. EDITORIAL LIMIT: This is an anti-hylomorphic result within the Tajrīd, not equivalent to the mutakallimūn’s atomism.

extracts.title: Kashf al-murād — reductio
extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: فإن كانت مادة كل جزء حادثة بعد القسمة لزمه التسلسل لأن كل حادث عندهم لا بد له من مادة
extracts.english: If each part’s matter comes to exist after division, a regress follows, since according to the opponents every newly originated thing requires matter.
extracts.source_line: Kashf al-murād, p.230, Ḥasanzāda Āmulī ed. (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: A distinct matter for each result of division creates a dilemma: infinitely many already actual matters or an infinite regress of generated matters. EDITORIAL LIMIT: The printed page transition places the continuation under the next heading; use p.229–230 together.

extracts.author: al-Jurjānī explaining al-Ījī

extracts.arabic: إذ على تقدير ثبوته لا صورة ولا هيولى ولا ما يتركب منهما

extracts.title: al-Nahal wa-l-ʿAlal fī taḥqīq aqsām al-ʿilal — distinction
extracts.author: Taşköprüzāde
extracts.arabic: فالغاية أعم من العلة الغائية
extracts.english: The end is more general than the final cause.
extracts.source_line: al-Nahal wa-l-ʿAlal fī taḥqīq aqsām al-ʿilal, critical text p.45 (Üçer ed.) (exact URL in source_url)

extracts.author: Taşköprüzāde
extracts.arabic: ويسمى فاعلاً كاملاً في الفاعلية، وهو المبدأ الأول

extracts.title: Kashf al-murād — distinction
extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.arabic: لكن تلك الصفات نفس الذات في الحقيقة وإن كانت مغايرة لها بالاعتبار
extracts.english: But these attributes are in reality identical with the Essence, although conceptually distinct from it.

extracts.title: Fuṣūṣ al-ḥikam — claim
extracts.author: Ibn ʿArabī
extracts.arabic: لأن الأعيان التي لها العدم الثابتة فيه ما شمَّت رائحة من الموجود
extracts.english: For the entities whose nonexistence remains established have not so much as smelled existence.
extracts.source_line: Fuṣūṣ al-ḥikam, p.76, ʿAfīfī ed. (exact URL in source_url)
extracts.notes: Fixed entities must not be casually redescribed as independently existing essences; they are known determinations, not created existing things. extracts.title: Miftāḥ ghayb al-jamʿ — claim
extracts.author: Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī

extracts.title: One certain existential judgment despite uncertainty about cause
extracts.english: When we consider something originated, we are certain it has a cause while remaining uncertain whether that cause is necessary or contingent.
extracts.arabic: إذا نظرنا في الحادث جزمنا بأنّ له مؤثرا مع التردّد في كونه واجبا أو ممكنا.
extracts.notes: The later part of the page records an objection to the equivocal term one-of-the-existences and refines the argument by persistence of the same existential assent despite changing categorial judgment.
extracts.source_line: شوارق الإلهام في شرح تجريد الكلام, I, p. 131. Direct Arabic HTML transcription checked 2026-10-30; print witness and manuscript variants not collated.

extracts.title: A universal concept is not thereby an additional extramental being
extracts.english: The concept of existence is not one of the [external] existents; rather it is among intelligibles in the mind.
extracts.arabic: مفهوم الوجود ليس من الموجودات، بل هو من المعقولات الذّهنيّة.
extracts.notes: The printed page attributes one reply to Qūshjī through a note; Lāhījī supplies the surrounding argument. Do not transfer Lāhījī’s prose to Qūshjī.

extracts.title: Shared existence cannot be the genus of all essences
extracts.english: If existence were a part of every quiddity, it would be a part shared among them.
extracts.arabic: إذا كان الوجود جزءا من كل ماهية، فإنه يكون جزءا مشتركا بينها.
extracts.notes: This is the initial premise of a reductio. Al-Ḥillī then argues that treating it as a genus forces new differentiae, and those differentiae again require existence, leading to an infinite regress. The modern footnote is not his own text.
extracts.source_line: كشف المراد في شرح تجريد الاعتقاد, p. 35. Direct Arabic HTML transcription checked 2026-10-30; print witness and manuscript variants not collated.

extracts.title: Essence understood while its existence is uncertain
extracts.english: We may understand a quiddity while doubting whether it exists in the mind or externally.
extracts.arabic: إنّا قد نعقل الماهية ونشك في وجودها الذهني والخارجي.
extracts.notes: The argument establishes a difference at the conceptual level; it does not on its own entail a real accident of existence inhering in an independently actual essence.

extracts.notes: This is Al-Ḥillī’s fifth proof. The surrounding page also contains arguments from informative predication and from true negative existential predication.

extracts.title: The persisting possible requires its cause
extracts.english: A possible being that persists continues to require its cause, since the ground of that need persists.
extracts.arabic: والممكن الباقي مفتقر إلى المؤثر لوجود علته.
extracts.notes: The page marks this as قال; the explanation beginning أقول is al-Ḥillī’s. The pronoun in علته refers to the cause of needing a cause (possibility).

extracts.title: Preservation is the causal contribution after origination
extracts.english: Its efficacy after originating the thing concerns a further feature, namely continued existence.
extracts.arabic: وتأثيره بعد الإحداث في أمر جديد هو البقاء.
extracts.notes: Al-Ḥillī reports a dilemma: the cause either re-produces the already existing state (absurd) or causes a new state (not the old thing). His response distinguishes preserving the effect from re-originating the very same completed production.
extracts.source_line: كشف المراد في شرح تجريد الاعتقاد, p. 77, Zanjānī edition of Kashf. Direct Arabic HTML transcription checked 2026-10-30; print witness and manuscript variants not collated.

extracts.title: Persistence as continuous bestowal, not replacement
extracts.english: What we mean by persistence is the uninterrupted continuance of the bestowal of existence.
extracts.arabic: مرادنا من البقاء هو استمرار فيض الوجود على سبيل الاتصال.
extracts.notes: This treatment excludes an interrupted succession of newly recreated replicas, and identifies persistence with an uninterrupted influx. The printed text is a distinct edition from Asad ʿAlīzāda; keep pagination separate.
extracts.source_line: شوارق الإلهام في شرح تجريد الكلام, I, p. 138, Mahdavī edition of Shawāriq. Direct Arabic HTML transcription checked 2026-10-30; print witness and manuscript variants not collated.

extracts.title: The decisive counterexample of persistent heat
extracts.english: Why, then, could it not remain by itself after its cause had rendered it preponderant?
extracts.arabic: فلم لا يجوز ان يكون قد بقي بنفسه بعد ان يرجح بعلته.
extracts.notes: Lāhījī first reproduces Jurjānī’s continuous causal defence and then asks this objection in his own voice (وأقول). He adduces heat remaining in water after removal of a fire, against the light analogy. Do not attribute this objection to Jurjānī.
extracts.source_line: شوارق الإلهام في شرح تجريد الكلام, I, p. 139, Mahdavī edition of Shawāriq. Direct Arabic HTML transcription checked 2026-10-30; print witness and manuscript variants not collated.

extracts.title: Existence-bestowing cause as ontological following
extracts.english: What is meant by causation and the bestowal of existence is consequential dependence [the effect following upon its cause].
extracts.arabic: المراد من العلية وإفادة الوجود هو الاستتباع.
extracts.notes: Lāhījī distinguishes dependence on an existence-bestowing cause from dependence on a preparatory condition. He explicitly calls the causal being of the contingent existence-through-another, not self-existence. Does not establish a specifically Thomistic account of secondary agency.
extracts.source_line: شوارق الإلهام في شرح تجريد الكلام, I, p. 140, Mahdavī edition of Shawāriq. Direct Arabic HTML transcription checked 2026-10-30; print witness and manuscript variants not collated.

extracts.title: Natural agents classified as preparatory causes
extracts.english: Fire, the sun, and the other natural agents are only preparatory causes.
extracts.arabic: والنار والشمس وساير المؤثرات الطبيعيّة انما هي معدّات.
extracts.notes: For this passage Lāhījī views natural agents as preparations for forms bestowed by a separate principle; it should NOT be cited as direct agreement with Aquinas on created secondary efficient causation.

extracts.title: Meaning of voluntary agency in the eternity debate
extracts.section: distinction of intent and intrinsic volition
extracts.english: The philosophers deny intention in the Necessary because they regard intention as choice additional to the essence.
extracts.arabic: الحكماء ينفون القصد عن الواجب لأنهم يجعلون القصد بالاختيار الزائد على الذات.
extracts.notes: Lāhījī distinguishes additional purposive intention from intrinsic divine satisfaction/volition. This is a polemical reconstruction of philosopher terminology, not proof that all scholastic accounts of free agency are equivalent.
extracts.source_line: شوارق الإلهام في شرح تجريد الكلام, I, p. 141, Mahdavī edition of Shawāriq. Direct Arabic HTML transcription checked 2026-10-30; print witness and manuscript variants not collated.

extracts.title: Conceded broad material receptivity does not settle prime matter
extracts.english: There is no dispute about something falling under the broad notion of matter [as receptive].
extracts.arabic: لا نزاع ... في ثبوت ما يصدق عليه مفهوم الهيولى بالمعنى الأعمّ.

extracts.title: Which reality fulfils the receptive role?
extracts.english: The dispute is not whether matter exists in this sense, but what this concept applies to.
extracts.arabic: الخلاف ليس في ثبوت مفهوم الهيولى والمادّة بهذا المعنى، بل فيما يصدق عليه هذا المفهوم.
extracts.notes: Candidates: indivisible atoms, hard small bodies, the body itself, or something simpler than body that is one of its components. The passage avoids a false matter-versus-no-receptivity binary.
extracts.source_line: شوارق الإلهام في شرح تجريد الكلام, III, p. 145. Direct Arabic HTML transcription checked 2026-10-30; print witness and manuscript variants not collated.

extracts.english: Rather, it is wholly simple, self-subsisting and not in a substrate, yet capable of undergoing division.

extracts.title: Substantial versus quantitative continuity
extracts.english: The second [sense] is that something, in its very essence, is capable of acquiring connectedness in the first sense.
extracts.arabic: ثانيهما: كون الشّيء في حدّ ذاته بحيث يعرضه الإتّصال بالمعنى الأوّل.
extracts.notes: The first sense is geometric continuum with shared boundaries; the second is substantial extended reality receptive to geometric determination. The proof shifts if they are conflated.
extracts.source_line: شوارق الإلهام في شرح تجريد الكلام, III, p. 148. Direct Arabic HTML transcription checked 2026-10-30; print witness and manuscript variants not collated.

extracts.title: Separation varies with continuity
extracts.english: Separation too, as the opposite of continuity, is divided according to the divisions of continuity.

extracts.title: Burden of proof: substantial intrinsic continuum
extracts.english: The affirmation or denial of prime matter turns upon whether substantial continuity is established.

extracts.title: Some material persistence through division
extracts.english: A body does not perish altogether, leaving nothing remaining, when separation occurs to it.
extracts.arabic: أنّ الجسم بطريان الانفصال عليه لا ينعدم بالكلّية بحيث لا يبقى منه شيء.

extracts.english: Division will accordingly be the transformation of one existence into two.
extracts.arabic: فيكون الانفصال تحوّل وجود واحد إلى وجودين.
extracts.notes: If intrinsic continuity is a thing’s own existence and individuality, division ends that numerically one connected substance. Whether this assumption holds is separately contested.

extracts.title: Where matter and corporeal form enter
extracts.english: The inhering constituent is what is termed corporeal form, and the substrate is what is termed matter.
extracts.arabic: فالحال هو المسمّى بالصّورة الجسميّة، والمحلّ هو المسمّى بالهيولى.
extracts.notes: Lāhījī immediately tests a difficulty about substrate neither intrinsically connected nor divided, replying on the Peripatetic account that the corporeal form has priority in existence. This does not settle Ṭūsī’s regress challenge.
extracts.source_line: شوارق الإلهام في شرح تجريد الكلام, III, p. 154. Direct Arabic HTML transcription checked 2026-10-30; print witness and manuscript variants not collated.

extracts.title: Later direct rebuttal to Ṭūsī’s infinite-substrates argument
extracts.english: Matter is one when continuity is one, and multiple when continuity is multiple.
extracts.arabic: المادّة واحدة عند وحدة الاتّصال، ومتعدّدة عند تعدّده.
extracts.notes: Astarābādī responds to the reductio that distinct matter for divided pieces must already exist as actually infinite matter within the undivided whole. He asserts numerical plurality can follow division rather than precede it.

extracts.english: There must therefore be some further thing shared by the original continuum and the two resulting continua.

extracts.title: Astarābādī endorses two physical constituents
extracts.english: Body as such is composed of these two, and this is called a natural body.
extracts.arabic: الجسم المطلق مركّب منهما، وذلك يسمّى جسما طبيعيّا.
extracts.notes: The two are the receptive prime matter and the connected corporeal form; the page separates natural body from mathematical body as three-dimensional quantity.

extracts.english: Know that the purpose [here] is to invalidate the argument. Nevertheless, the truth is that existence is a simple meaning, having neither external nor intellectual parts, as will be explained.

extracts.english: This additional concept would be an intelligible consideration existing only in the intellect, whereas that of which it is predicated would be an actual, external existent: the reality of existence.

extracts.english: Reply: although apprehending [the quiddity] consists in its existence in the mind, apprehending it is not the same as apprehending its existence in the mind.

extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.arabic: وذلك كما أن التلفظ بلفظ زيد، وجود لفظي لذات زيد، لكنه وجود خارجي لذلك اللفظ لا محالة، وكذلك نقش هذا اللفظ في الكتابة وجود كتبي لهذا اللفظ، ووجود خارجي لذلك النقش.
extracts.english: It is like uttering the word ‘Zayd’: this is a verbal existence of Zayd himself, yet it is necessarily external existence for the uttered word. Similarly, writing that word gives the word written existence, while the inscription itself has external existence.
extracts.title: Shawāriq al-ilhām fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-kalām, Asad ʿAlīzāda edition — I:219

extracts.english: It thereby becomes evident that the cognitive image genuinely belongs to the category of quality, and not only figuratively, by treating mental things as resembling extramental things, as the investigator Dawwānī held.

extracts.english: As for [the rational soul’s] substantiality, it follows from its immateriality: namely, its subsisting in itself and not inhering in matter.

extracts.author: Ibn Sīnā (quoted by al-Lāhījī)
extracts.arabic: فإن جعلت هذه المعقولات أجزاء ذاته، عرض التكثر في ذاته تعالى، وإن جعلتها لواحق ذاته، عرض لذاته أن لا يكون من جهتها واجب الوجود.
extracts.english: If these intelligibles are made parts of His essence, multiplicity arises in the divine essence. If they are made concomitants of His essence, it follows that in their respect His essence is not necessary in existence.

extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.arabic: ولا يجوز أن يكون بالصور القائمة بذواتها أو بذات المعلول الأول، وإلا لكانت هذه الصور من جملة تلك الموجودات فيكون نظامها لا عن علم، أو عن علم آخر، ويتسلسل.
extracts.english: Nor may [His knowledge ordering existence] consist in forms subsisting by themselves or in the essence of the first effect. Otherwise these forms themselves would belong to the ordered existents, and their order would either not arise from knowledge or would require further knowledge, generating a regress.

extracts.english: Among the indications that God’s knowledge does not differ before and after things come to exist is that it remains in one state from eternity to eternity, and does not change as what is known passes from nonexistence to existence.

extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.work: Shawāriq al-ilhām fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-kalām
extracts.arabic: إنّا نحكم حكما إيجابيّا على ما لا تحقق له في الخارج أصلا، كقولنا: اجتماع النقيضين مستلزم لكلّ منهما ومغاير لاجتماع الضدّين.
extracts.english: We make an affirmative judgment about what has no actuality at all outside the mind; for example, we say that a conjunction of contradictories entails each of its members and is distinct from a conjunction of contraries.
extracts.argument: Explicitly states the positive-judgment problem for impossibilities. The intellectual object of predication cannot simply be identified with an external subject.

extracts.english: Know that this objection can be formulated with reference to the act of affirming (ithbāt), or with reference to the obtaining of what is affirmed (thubūt).
extracts.argument: Separates logical assertion from ontological establishment; stops argument from the truth of a judgment to an independent realm of established impossibles.

extracts.work: Shawāriq al-ilhām fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-kalām

extracts.english: For the criterion of truth in a judgment employing conceptual or relational considerations is its correspondence with what obtains in itself (nafs al-amr), as the book will later explain.
extracts.argument: Directly gives a correspondence criterion for objective truth in judgments whose predicates are iʿtibārī, linking Q09 and Q10.

extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.work: Shawāriq al-ilhām fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-kalām
extracts.arabic: ليس غرض الشيخ من كون الإمكان معنى موجودا أنّ الإمكان صفة وجودية، أي موجودة في الخارج بنفسها؛ بل غرضه أنّه معنى موجود أي له منشأ انتزاع في الوجود الخارجي.
extracts.english: Avicenna does not mean, in calling possibility an existent meaning, that possibility is a positive property subsisting outside the mind in its own right. Rather he means that it is a meaningful determination abstracted from a basis in extra-mental existence.
extracts.argument: Lāhījī offers a reading of Avicenna that separates the modal attribution from an externally inhering modal entity.
extracts.limitations: Arabic transcription inspected on an identifiable text page; short excerpt only, no manuscript or printed-image variants collated. Reported interpretation of Ibn Sīnā by Lāhījī, not an independent Ibn Sīnā quotation.

extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.work: Shawāriq al-ilhām fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-kalām
extracts.arabic: ومعنى ارتفاع النقيضين في المفردات هو أن لا يصدقا على شيء ... وليس معناه خلوّ النقيضين عن الوجود والثبوت في أنفسهما.
extracts.english: The meaning of both contradictories being absent in the case of terms is that neither is truly predicable of anything; it is not that the two opposed concepts lack existence or establishment in themselves.
extracts.argument: Answers an objection claiming that if modal terms are conceptual, two contradictory modal predications would both be nonexistent. Distinguishes term-level predication and property existence.

extracts.author: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī (lemma quoted by al-Ḥillī)
extracts.work: Tajrīd al-kalām as quoted in Kashf al-murād
extracts.arabic: فالحركة كمالٌ أوّلُ لما بالقوّة من حيث هو بالقوّة، أو حصول الجسم في مكان بعد آخر.
extracts.english: Motion is the first actuality of something potential precisely inasmuch as it is potential—or, in the second definition, a body’s occupying one place after another.
extracts.argument: Ṭūsī presents in compressed form distinct Aristotelian and kalām definitions of motion; the controversy must start with the two rival definitions.

extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.work: Kashf al-murād fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-iʿtiqād
extracts.arabic: هذان تعريفان للحركة: الأوّل منهما للحكماء، والثاني للمتكلّمين ... وإنّما قيّدنا بقولنا من حيث هو بالقوّة لأنّ الحركة تفارق سائر الكمالات.
extracts.english: These are two definitions of motion: the first is that of the philosophers and the second that of the theologians. The qualification “insofar as it is potential” is required because motion differs from other actualizations.
extracts.argument: Al-Ḥillī explicitly distinguishes physical actuality-in-process from a simple change of place and explains the remaining potentiality inherent in an ongoing motion.

extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.work: Kashf al-murād fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-iʿtiqād
extracts.arabic: وجود الحركة يتوقّف على أمور ستّة: أحدها ما منه الحركة، والثاني ما إليه الحركة ... الثالث ما به الحركة ... الرابع ما له الحركة ... الخامس ما فيه الحركة ... السادس الزمان الذي تقع فيه الحركة.
extracts.english: The existence of motion depends on six terms: its point of departure; its terminus; that by which it occurs, its efficient cause; that to which it belongs, the moving body as receptive cause; that in which it occurs, its category; and the time in which it occurs.
extracts.argument: Movement is not a free-floating succession of states; there is a bearer, causal principle, domain, endpoints and temporal measure.
extracts.limitations: Arabic transcription inspected on an identifiable text page; short excerpt only, no manuscript or printed-image variants collated. Ellipses omit Ḥillī’s explanatory appositions which have been rendered in the English translation.
extracts.status: online Arabic transcription inspected; translation prepared; manuscript readings unchecked

extracts.author: al-Ḥillī
extracts.work: Kashf al-murād fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-iʿtiqād
extracts.arabic: والحركة تقع في أربع مقولات لا غير، هي الكمّ والكيف والأين والوضع ... وأمّا الجوهر فقسمان بسيط ومركّب، فالبسيط يوجد دفعة فلا تتحقّق فيه حركة.
extracts.english: Motion occurs in four categories and no others—quantity, quality, place and position. As for substance, the simple comes to be all at once, so there is no motion within it.
extracts.argument: Shows why the inherited tradition excludes substance from the categories admitting gradual motion, setting up the precise challenge of Ṣadrian substantial motion.
extracts.limitations: Arabic transcription inspected on an identifiable text page; short excerpt only, no manuscript or printed-image variants collated. Ellipsis omits a classification of composite substances, addressed in the accompanying essay.
extracts.status: online Arabic transcription inspected; translation prepared; manuscript readings unchecked

extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.work: Shawāriq al-ilhām fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-kalām
extracts.arabic: الحركة في كلّ شيء معناها أن يكون المتحرّك متقوّما وموجودا من دون ذلك الشيء وباقيا بعينه، ويتوارد عليه في كلّ آن من الآنات المفروضة في زمان الحركة فرد من أفراد ذلك الشيء.
extracts.english: Motion in a given determination requires a moving subject already constituted and existent without that determination, persisting as the same subject while successive instances of the determination occur in the posited instants of the motion.
extracts.argument: Provides the hidden substrate-persistence premise behind rejecting motion in a quiddity’s own existence.
extracts.limitations: Arabic transcription inspected on an identifiable text page; short excerpt only, no manuscript or printed-image variants collated. The old-pagination digital transcription differs from Asad ʿAlīzāda five-volume pagination.
extracts.status: online Arabic transcription inspected; translation prepared; manuscript readings unchecked

extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.work: Shawāriq al-ilhām fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-kalām
extracts.arabic: فلو تحرّكت الماهية في الوجود لزم أن يكون جميع أفراد وجودها في زمان الحركة بالقوّة، فيلزم كون الماهية حال الحركة في الوجود موجودة بالقوّة لا بالفعل.
extracts.english: If quiddity were moving in existence, all the successive instances of its existence throughout the motion would have to be potential. It would follow that, while it moved in existence, the quiddity would be potential rather than actual.
extracts.argument: Second objection to motion in existence, distinct from the substrate argument: the existence of the moving subject cannot consist exclusively in unactualized successive existences.
extracts.limitations: Arabic transcription inspected on an identifiable text page; short excerpt only, no manuscript or printed-image variants collated.

extracts.author: Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī
extracts.work: Masāʾil al-murāsalāt maʿa Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī
extracts.arabic: والذي أفادته المعاينة المحقّقة والذوق الصحيح هو أنّ الماهيات غير مجعولة وأنّ لها ضربا من الوجود، وهو من حيث اعتبار تعيّنها في علم الحقّ أزلا وأبدا على وتيرة واحدة.
extracts.english: What verified direct apprehension and sound spiritual tasting disclose, however, is that the quiddities are not made, and that they have a mode of being, considered in their determination within God’s knowledge, eternally and without change.
extracts.argument: Qūnawī formulates the core fixed-entities hypothesis as noncreated determination in divine knowledge; it is not simply a thesis that independent nonexistents stand outside God.
extracts.limitations: Arabic transcription inspected on an identifiable text page; short excerpt only, no manuscript or printed-image variants collated.
extracts.status: online Arabic transcription inspected; translation prepared; manuscript readings unchecked

extracts.author: Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī
extracts.work: Masāʾil al-murāsalāt maʿa Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī
extracts.arabic: فإن حكم بثبوت الأمر فمن وجه آخر، لأنّا نعلم أنّ علم الحقّ في مقام أحديّته عين ذاته، فلا تعدّد هناك إلّا باعتبار التعلّقات.
extracts.english: If one judges this matter to be established, it is from another consideration: we know that the knowledge of the Real, in the station of His oneness, is identical with His essence. There is no multiplicity there except with respect to the relations of knowledge.
extracts.argument: Qūnawī denies that the plurality of known quiddities entails a plurality in the divine essence; the many determinations belong to relations, not essential parts.
extracts.limitations: Arabic transcription inspected on an identifiable text page; short excerpt only, no manuscript or printed-image variants collated.

extracts.author: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī
extracts.work: Masāʾil al-murāsalāt maʿa Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī
extracts.arabic: والقول بأنّ الماهيات العارية عن الوجودين العقلي والعيني لها ثبوت وتميّز، أو ثبوت بلا تميّز، قول بأنّ المعدوم شيء، وهو مذهب المثبتين من المعتزلة.
extracts.english: To claim that quiddities deprived of both intellectual and external existence nevertheless have establishment and differentiation—or establishment without differentiation—is to hold that the nonexistent is a thing, the doctrine of those Muʿtazilites who affirm its establishment.
extracts.argument: Ṭūsī disallows a third objective mode of established quiddity independently of mental and external existence; he understands such a thesis as bordering on the Muʿtazilī nonexistent-as-thing.
extracts.limitations: Arabic transcription inspected on an identifiable text page; short excerpt only, no manuscript or printed-image variants collated. The point at issue is whether this objection engages Qūnawī’s relational qualification adequately; it is not a refutation of every possible Akbarī reconstruction.
extracts.status: online Arabic transcription inspected; translation prepared; manuscript readings unchecked

extracts.author: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī
extracts.work: Masāʾil al-murāsalāt maʿa Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī
extracts.arabic: القول بأنّ الماهيات غير مجعولة وأنّ لها ضربا من الوجود قريب من قول مثبتَي المعتزلة ... ولعلّ مولانا ... أراد به شيئا آخر لم يفهمه المريد المستفيد.
extracts.english: The claim that quiddities are unmade and possess a mode of existence is close to the position of the Muʿtazilites who affirm established nonexistents. Perhaps, however, our master intended something else that his student, eager to learn, has not understood.
extracts.argument: Crucially, Ṭūsī explicitly suspends the claim that he has fully grasped Qūnawī’s meaning. The text is not a simple declaration that the two thinkers teach identical theses, nor a fully resolved refutation.
extracts.limitations: Arabic transcription inspected on an identifiable text page; short excerpt only, no manuscript or printed-image variants collated. Ellipsis marks the courteous address omitted between the two translated clauses.

extracts.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Lāhījī
extracts.work: Shawāriq al-ilhām fī sharḥ Tajrīd al-kalām
extracts.arabic: والمراد بالأفراد الذهنية هو الأفراد المقدّرة على أن يكون الذهن ظرفا للوجود الفرضي، أعني الوجود الذي هو نفس الفرض والتقدير في الذهن.
extracts.english: By “mental individuals” is meant individuals supposed such that the intellect is the place of their hypothetical existence—that is, the existence constituted by intellectual supposition and positing itself.
extracts.argument: The ontological cost of a true universal proposition is less than the cost of positing an extra-mental instance of its subject; this frames correspondence and logical scope.
extracts.limitations: Arabic transcription inspected on an identifiable text page; short excerpt only, no manuscript or printed-image variants collated. The source carefully distinguishes two senses of “mentally existing individual”; it does not on its own demonstrate a divine locus of nafs al-amr.

extracts.title: Existence as a unified reality differing by perfection
extracts.english: For if existence has diverse realized realities, one may come to see that these realities do not differ in their entire reality, but rather in intensity and weakness. Existence would then be one reality, differentiated in its manifestations—which are the quiddities—according to intensity and weakness, perfection and deficiency.
extracts.arabic: فإنه إذا كان للوجود حقائق مختلفة متحققة ويمكن أن يتفطن بكون تلك الحقائق غير مختلفة بتمام الحقيقة، بل بالشدة والضعف. فيكون الوجود حقيقة واحدة متفاوتة في المظاهر التي هي الماهيات بحسب الشدة والضعف، والكمال والنقص.
notes: Lāhījī initially formulates a potential interpretation, not his final demonstration of numerical unity.

extracts.title: The philosophical/Sufi contrast: under a condition versus without a condition
extracts.english: The difference between this position and that of the philosophers would be that the philosophers restrict necessity to one rank: that reality on condition that it not become determined by any of the quiddities. The Sufis, by contrast, assign necessity to that reality without making its non-determination by any quiddity a condition.
extracts.arabic: فيكون الفرق بين هذا المذهب، ومذهب الحكماء، انهم يخصون الواجبية بمرتبة واحدة؛ هي تلك الحقيقة بشرط أن لا يتعين بشيء من الماهيات. والصوفية يجعلون الواجبية لتلك الحقيقة؛ لا بشرط أن يتعين بشيء من الماهيات.
notes: This proposal turns on bi-sharṭ lā versus lā bi-sharṭ; those logical qualifications cannot be collapsed into a physical division of one substance.

extracts.title: Objection: a self-subsisting existence does not exclude dependent existences
extracts.english: But whence does it follow that no existence other than this can subsist through contingent quiddities, and that every existential reality must subsist through itself? What was said about existence having to be a genuine particular applies only to an existential reality subsisting in itself.
extracts.arabic: فمن أين يلزم أنه لا يكون وجود غير ذلك قائما بالماهيات الممكنة وأن يكون كل حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها؟ وما ذكر من وجوب كون الوجود جزئيا حقيقيا، إنما هو في حقيقة وجودية قائمة بذاتها.
notes: This is a direct logical challenge to an inference from a unique necessary self-subsistent being to the denial of all dependent particular existences.

extracts.title: Universal absolute existence is an intellectual predicate
extracts.english: Absolute existence is not an objective attribute in the sense of existing outside the mind; rather, it is an intellectual attribute that exists only in the intellect. The author indicates this by saying: existence—that is, absolute existence—is among the intellectual predicates.
extracts.arabic: أن الوجود المطلق ليست بصفة عينية بمعنى كونها موجودة في الخارج، بل هي صفة عقلية موجودة في العقل فقط. وإليه أشار المصنف بقوله: والوجود، أي المطلق من المحمولات العقلية.
notes: Neither the intellectual universality of the term nor its second-intelligible status settles the extra-mental plurality or unity of the subjects.

extracts.title: Trilemma against gradation of what is essential
extracts.english: In sum, if gradation by intensity or increase is supposed to occur in what belongs to a thing essentially, three alternatives arise. First, the more intense or greater contains nothing that the weaker or lesser lacks; in that case there is no gradation, whether essential or otherwise. Second, it contains something of this kind included within the concept shared by the gradated cases; then the weaker cannot share that concept, since it lacks part of it. Third, it contains such a difference outside the concept. This does not exclude gradation altogether, but it does exclude gradation in what is essential.
extracts.arabic: والحاصل أنه على تقدير وقوع التشكيك بالشدة أو الزيادة في الذاتي ثلاث احتمالات: الأول: أن لا يشتمل الأشد والأزيد على أمر ليس في الأضعف والأنقص. وهذا يستلزم أن لا يكون هاهنا تشكيك أصلا لا في الذاتي ولا في غيره. الثاني: أن يتحقق ذلك الأمر ويكون داخلا في مفهوم المشكك؛ وهذا يستلزم عدم اشتراكهما ضرورة انتفاء جزئه في الأضعف. الثالث: أن يتحقق ويكون خارجا عن مفهومه. هذا وإن لم يستلزم انتفاء التشكيك مطلقا، لكنه يستلزم انتفاء التشكيك في الذاتي.
notes: The disagreement distinguishes essential definition from differentiation in extrinsic determinations or predicates; not yet a source for full Dawwānī–Dashtakī exchange.

extracts.title: Gradation of individuals and application of a derivative predicate
extracts.english: In short, a universal whose individuals differ in intensity and increase is not, on that account, itself predicated gradationally, because the differentiation occurs among its individuals in themselves rather than in the truth of the universal of them. Admittedly, the difference among the individuals can yield a differential application of the derivative predicate formed from that universal to the subjects possessing those individuals.
extracts.arabic: وبالجملة: فالكلي الذي تتفاوت أفراده بالشدة والزيادة لا يكون مشككا، إذ التفاوت بين أفراده بالذات لا في صدق هذا الكلي عليها. نعم، التفاوت الواقع بين أفراده بالذات يوجب تفاوت صدق المشتق من هذا الكلي على معروضات تلك الأفراد.
notes: Prevents reading distinct intensities of blackness as though the definition of blackness were numerically different in each predicate application.

extracts.title: What makes an external attribution true?
extracts.english: Al-Sayyid al-Sanad said: If that statement corresponds to the truth, the subject is actually qualified by the predicate externally. The mere external presence of a body and of whiteness does not suffice to establish the relevant relation between them: otherwise it would be true that a Black person is externally qualified by whiteness merely because both that person and whiteness exist outside the mind. But if the statement is false, it carries no weight.
extracts.arabic: قال السيد السند: تلك الحكاية، إن كانت صادقة كان متصفا في الخارج به، ولا يكفي في ذلك وجود الجسم والبياض فيه لعلاقة بينهما فيه، وإلا لصدق أن الزنجي متصف بالبياض في الخارج لوجود الزنجي والبياض كليهما فيه، وإن كان كاذبا فلا عبرة.
notes: Supersedes blanket Jurjānī attribution: p.12 n.6 explicitly identifies al-Sayyid al-Sanad as Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Dashtakī; n.8 distinguishes Jurjānī as al-Muḥaqqiq al-Sharīf.
The p.33 passage itself lacks a fresh identifying note. Dashtakī is contextually probable, not independently confirmed from his original gloss.
Printed Arabic has وإن كان كاذبا فلا عبرة, with masculine كان; the inherited transcription is retained here and C31Y02 supplies the subsequent argument.

extracts.title: Reply: the relation of qualification need not itself be an external existent
extracts.english: I answer: we choose the first alternative and say that there is between them in the external order a relation, namely qualification (ittiṣāf), but it does not exist in the external order. His words, “but they are in the external order in a certain manner,” point to this.
extracts.arabic: قلت: نختار الأول ونقول: إن بينهما في الخارج علاقة هي الاتصاف، لكنها ليست موجودة في الخارج. وقوله قدس سره: «لكنهما في الخارج على وجه»، إشارة إلى هذا.
notes: Literal distinction retained: “in the external order” versus “exists in the external order.” The earlier “independently existing” was an explanatory addition, not explicit Arabic.

extracts.title: The external existent as concept and mental predication
extracts.english: A better response is to say that the concept “externally existent” is predicated of its instances insofar as they are present in the intellect, not insofar as they exist outside it; otherwise their existence there would have to precede the applicability of that concept to them.
extracts.arabic: والوجه أن يقال أن مفهوم الموجود الخارجي إنما يصدق على أفراده حال كونها موجودة في الذهن لا في الخارج؛ وإلا لزم تقدم وجودها فيه على صدقه عليها.
notes: Selected continuous sentence only, not the earlier draft’s inaccurate composite.
On the epistemic site of predication, not a denial of extramental things.

extracts.title: Nafs al-amr and the active intellect: exemplification rather than exclusivity
extracts.english: I say: It is possible that the active intellect is mentioned not as an exclusive identification, but as an illustration. For it appears that all [higher] principles stand on the same footing in this respect; indeed divine knowledge is more exalted and higher, and therefore has a still stronger claim to be regarded as actuality and *nafs al-amr*.
extracts.arabic: أقول: ويجوز أن لا يكون ذكر خصوص العقل الفعال للحصر، بل للتمثيل؛ فإن الظاهر أن المبادئ كلها في هذا المعنى سواء، بل علم الله تعالى أجل وأعلى، فهو بكونه الواقع ونفس الأمر أحق.
notes: Rejects the inference “nafs al-amr = only the active intellect”; his argument invokes a hierarchy of cognitional foundations. Need distinguish ontological truthmaker from merely comparing representations.

extracts.title: The continued effect requires its cause because possibility remains
extracts.english: The philosophers and the later theologians held that a contingent being which persists remains in need of an agent. The reason is that the cause of its needing an agent is its possibility; and that possibility still obtains during its persistence.
extracts.arabic: ذهب الحكماء والمتأخرون من المتكلمين إلى أن الممكن الباقي مفتقر إلى المؤثر؛ وذلك لأن علة حاجته إلى المؤثر هو الإمكان، وهو حال البقاء حاصل.
notes: Ascribes the causal need to metaphysical possibility rather than merely to temporal origination; this is a lemma, not a proof that every natural cause is preparatory.

extracts.title: Persistence dilemma: what new work does a cause perform?
extracts.english: If what persists needed an agent while persisting, either that agent would have some causal effect upon it or it would not. On the opponent’s view each alternative is impossible.
extracts.arabic: لو افتقر الباقي في حال بقائه إلى المؤثر، فالمؤثر: إما أن يكون له فيه تأثير أو لا يكون، وكلاهما محال.
notes: Correct speaker: this is al-Iṣfahānī **reporting an objection**, not necessarily endorsing it. It motivates the distinction between a newly caused entity and the continued being of an existing entity.
SOURCE STATUS PROVISIONAL. Complete objector’s two-pronged reasoning still to be verified against printed text.

extracts.title: Response: the effect is continuation rather than first origination
extracts.english: The reply may be formulated as follows: while the effect persists the agent contributes something that is not the existence it already possessed before, but something new—namely, the persistence of that earlier existence—and thus it counts as persisting.
extracts.arabic: تقرير الجواب: أن المؤثر حال البقاء يفيد أثرا ليس هو الوجود الذي كان حاصلا قبل ذلك، بل أمرا جديدا هو بقاء الوجود الذي كان حاصلا قبل ذلك، وبه صار باقيا.
notes: This response distinguishes *ibqāʾ* from *ījād*; it must still face Lāhījī’s deeper challenge to whether preservation counts as an independently produced new state.

extracts.title: Al-Qūshjī’s three objections concerning existence, nonexistence and joint conception
extracts.english: Al-Qūshjī raised the following objections. First, the coexistence of opposites when one is predicated of the other is not impossible, so there is no need to excuse it by invoking different respects. What is impossible is for both opposites to be predicated of the same subject. Second, if existence and nonexistence were combined in one subject, making it both existent and nonexistent, the same excuse could be used: nonexistence is opposed to the existent as its negation, yet, since existence belongs to the subject, the two allegedly coexist. Third, if “both may be conceived together” means what the earlier commentator proposes, the word “together” would be redundant.
extracts.arabic: فأورد عليه الشارح القوشجي: «أما أولا: فلأن اجتماع المقابلين بعروض أحدهما للآخر ليس مستحيلا حتى يحتاج إلى الاعتذار بتغاير الجهة إنما المستحيل اجتماعهما بعروضهما لمحل واحد. وأما ثانيا: فإنه لو اجتمع الوجود والعدم في محل واحد بأن يكون موجودا ومعدوما معا، يمكن إجراء هذا العذر فيه، بأن يقال: العدم من حيث انه سلب الموجود مقابل له، ومن حيث ان الوجود عارض لمحله مجتمع معه. وأما ثالثا: فإنه لو كان معنى قوله: وقد يعقلان معا، ما ذكره، لكان لفظة معا لغوا».
notes: This is a full three-part objection by Qūshjī quoted verbatim within Lāhījī’s later commentary, which cites Sharḥ Tajrīd al-ʿaqāʾid p.23; direct Qūshjī book facsimile not yet collated.
The opponent is the old commentator’s explanation of Ṭūsī’s phrase; it is not an argument denying the principle of noncontradiction.

extracts.title: Priority and intensity are not interchangeable
extracts.author: Mullā ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazdī
extracts.source_line: Yazdī, printed p.12 (= PDF page 12), paragraphs on aqdamiyya and ashaddiyya
extracts.arabic: وأما التشكيك بالأقدمية فهو أن يكون صدق الكلي على بعض أفراده متقدما على صدقه على بعض آخر بالذات والعلية لا بالزمان. فإن تقدم صدق الإنسان على الأب على صدقه على الابن لا يسمى تشكيكا. وأما الأشدية فقد يفسر بأكثرية ظهور آثار الكلي في بعض الأفراد. وزيفه السيد السند بأنه يستلزم كون كثير من الذاتيات كالإنسان مثلا مقولا بالشدة والضعف لاختلاف أفرادها في استتباع الآثار؛ ثم اختار تفسيرها بما استفاده من كلام بهمنيار فهو ازدياد طبيعة العام فيها في بعض الأفراد دون بعض كالطويل بالقياس إلى الذراع والذراعين، والأسود بالقياس إلى الفحم والقير.
extracts.english: Gradation by precedence means that the universal's being true of some of its instances precedes its being true of others essentially and causally, rather than temporally. The prior application of “human” to the father rather than the son is not called gradation. Intensity has sometimes been explained as the more abundant manifestation of the universal's effects in certain instances. Al-Sayyid al-Sanad rejected this because it would entail that many essential predicates, such as “human,” are said with intensity and weakness, since their instances differ in the effects that follow from them. He instead chose an explanation drawn from Bahmanyār: an increase of the common nature in some instances rather than others, as with “long” in relation to one cubit and two cubits, and “black” in relation to charcoal and pitch.

extracts.title: The counter-objection to an account in terms of union
extracts.author: Yazdī reporting al-Sayyid al-Sanad and responding
extracts.source_line: Yazdī, printed p.33 (= PDF page 33), complete paragraph beginning ثم أقول
extracts.arabic: ثم أقول: قد اختار السيد السند ـ قدس سره ـ أن المحكي عنه هو اتحاد الموضوع مع مفهوم المحمول في الخارج. فنقول: إن كانت تلك الحكاية صادقة لزم وجود الاتحاد في الخارج، وأنه يستلزم إليه؛ وإن كانت كاذبة لم يعتبر. فإن اختار أن الاتحاد في الخارج لا أنه موجود في الخارج، فقد صار إلى ما ذكرناه سواء بسواء.
extracts.english: Then I say: al-Sayyid al-Sanad chose the view that what is represented is the subject's union with the concept of the predicate in the external order. We therefore say: if that representation is true, the existence of the union in the external order follows, and it entails [a regress: the printed text reads “to it”]; if it is false, it is disregarded. If he chooses to say that the union is in the external order, without saying that it exists in the external order, he has arrived at precisely what we stated.

The reply does not establish that predication is arbitrary. It distinguishes an externally grounded union from an added externally existing relational entity.

extracts.title: External qualification and the status of negative predicates
extracts.author: Mullā ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazdī
extracts.source_line: Yazdī p.33, sequence from فهو من حيث أنه ليس في الخارج through الذاتيات
extracts.arabic: قوله: «فهو من حيث أنه ليس في الخارج». أي لا يوجد فيه، وإلا فالاتصاف أيضا في الخارج. قوله: «ومن حيث إنه يستدعي ملاحظة أمر خارج عن الموضوع». لا وجوده، وإلا كان من قبيل حمل الإضافات من غير فوق. قوله: «فظهر أن مطابق الحكم الحملي قد يكون ذات الموضوع فقط كما في الذاتيات». وكذا العدميات، فإنها وإن استدعت ملاحظة أمر زائد لا يستدعي وجود أمر سوى ذات الموضوع. فإن الموجود في الخارج المحكي عنه هو الذات فحسب.
extracts.english: His words, “insofar as it is not in the external order”: that is, it does not exist there; otherwise qualification too is in the external order. His words, “insofar as it requires considering something outside the subject”: [considering it], rather than its existence; otherwise it would be like predicating relations without an “above.” His words, “It thus becomes clear that what corresponds to a predicative judgment may be the subject's essence alone, as in essential predicates”: the same applies to negative predicates. Although these require considering something additional, they do not require anything to exist besides the subject's essence. The externally existing thing that is represented is the essence alone.
